extracted.intended_audience: general newspaper readers and wartime news consumers (readers of Associated Press/Tass/Izvestia dispatches)
extracted.subtask_description: Writing and assembling newspaper dispatches about wartime operations—synthesizing official communiqués, field observer reports, casualty/equipment counts, and strategic context into dated, attributed news copy. Includes coverage across multiple fronts and incorporation of diplomatic/political statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attribution to official communiqués and agencies
rubrics_metrics.description: Use and attribute information to official sources: e.g., 'a Russian midday communique announced yesterday', 'Red Star said', 'Tass dispatch', 'The German High Command ... broadcast from Berlin', 'By the Associated Press'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Always identify the issuing agency/newspaper/command and use quotations or datelines when reporting their statements. Note the time and origin of the communique (e.g., 'midnight Moscow communique') to situate claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report conflicting accounts from opposing sides
rubrics_metrics.description: Present both sides' versions: Germans asserted advances and destroyed Soviet units, while Soviet communiqués described repulses, encirclements and heavy German losses ('The German High Command ... said German forces had driven the Red Army closer to Kharkov' vs. 'Red Star said ... The Germans are trying at all costs to break through to the city').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include and juxtapose contradictory claims; indicate discrepancies and, where possible, give context or signals about reliability (e.g., classic explanations for retreats, omissions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Include precise battlefield details and counts
rubrics_metrics.description: Supply numbers and concrete details: divisions involved, miles of drives, tanks and aircraft destroyed or captured, prisoners, guns and materiel (e.g., '375-mile winter drive', 'destroyed thirty-six tanks yesterday', 'captured 315 trucks, ten tractors, 570 freight cars').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report figures that sources provide, but indicate when counts are claims or estimates; avoid presenting unverified numbers as definitive if sourcing is partisan.

rubrics_metrics.name: Geographic situating with distances and directions
rubrics_metrics.description: Give specific locations and distances: e.g., 'fifteen miles southeast of Vyazma', 'Smolensk, 130 miles to the west', 'eighty miles northeast of Smolensk', 'south of Kharkov'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Place events with relative distances, compass directions, and named transport hubs/railways to convey operational significance and movement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explain strategic significance and objectives
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain why places/moves matter: e.g., 'Possession of the city a narrow escape corridor to Smolensk', 'Bely was captured ... Bely is eighty miles northeast of Smolensk and ... powerfully fortified'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Link tactical events to broader strategic aims (supply lines, encirclement, approaches to major cities) so readers understand operational consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use field observers and on-the-ground reports
rubrics_metrics.description: Incorporate reports from 'field observers' and local dispatches: e.g., 'Field observers said the Germans were falling back on prepared positions', 'Field observers said the Germans were falling back upon prepared positions around various settlements.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use observer testimony for scene detail and color, but attribute and, where appropriate, flag its provisional or anecdotal nature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Describe tactics, terrain, and defensive measures
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe how forces use terrain and defensive works: e.g., 'digging in tanks as pillboxes and utilizing streams and forests as defense lines', 'sappers in blowing up bridges', 'throwing large forces of tanks and motorized infantry into the battle'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detail employment of terrain, fortifications and engineering efforts to explain battlefield dynamics and why attacks succeed or stall.

rubrics_metrics.name: Note silences, editorial choices and propaganda context
rubrics_metrics.description: Report on what is omitted or not commented upon: e.g., 'There was no editorial comment, and the Kremlin remained silent', 'the Soviet press, which does not report anything about materials sent to the front'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Point out notable absences, editorial restraint, or state media practices to help readers assess reporting context and potential bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use clear datelines and timestamps
rubrics_metrics.description: Include datelines and dates: e.g., 'Moscow, March 11', 'London, March 11', 'By the Associated Press', and references to times ('midnight Moscow communique', 'evening and morning broadcasts').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Always place reports temporally and geographically so readers can track when and where reports originated, and whether they are contemporaneous or delayed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cover multiple theaters and link developments
rubrics_metrics.description: Switch and connect coverage across fronts: e.g., central front (Vyazma/Smolensk), southern front (Kharkov/Donets), and North African fronts (Mareth Line, Tunisia, Gafsa).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide summaries of activity on other fronts and draw links where events in one theater affect strategy or public perception in another.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include political/diplomatic statements and implications
rubrics_metrics.description: Report statements by political/diplomatic figures and their domestic/international implications: e.g., 'Admiral William H. Standley’s declaration', 'Welles’ Remarks Listed', 'Stimson said ... The cornered Axis armies got nowhere', 'reference to Willkie, Senator Connally'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include official pronouncements, note disputes among officials, and explain how these statements influence public understanding or diplomatic relations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report casualties, prisoners and incomplete casualty accounting
rubrics_metrics.description: Give casualty/prisoner information and flag incompleteness: e.g., 'Allies have taken more than 1,000 German and Italian prisoners', 'casualty reports ... are incomplete', 'received reports of 59 killed, 176 wounded and 2,007 missing'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publish best-available totals, but explicitly state uncertainty and provisional nature of casualty figures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Detail air and naval operations and their effects
rubrics_metrics.description: Include air/naval action reports: bomber and fighter strikes, ships and planes destroyed on ground, hits on ports/airfields (e.g., 'bombs were seen to burst over both air fields', 'Fortress crews bagged six of the eight Nazi fighters').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe platforms, targets, observed effects (fires, vehicles burning) and escort/support forces to convey operational impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use vivid but factual language to convey intensity
rubrics_metrics.description: Employ descriptive phrases to convey scale/intensity: e.g., 'battle rivaling the struggle at Stalingrad in bitterness and intensity', 'waged a ferocious engagement', 'heavy casualties were inflicted'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance vivid descriptors with sourced facts; avoid sensationalism that lacks attribution or evidence.
